content:
kevin_sre: Heads-up — our GPU health dashboard is showing a steady rise in correctable ECC and early Xid spikes on nodes in eu1-dedicated-pool-3. Not critical yet but trending. ops_bot: [alert] gpu-ecc-rate > baseline (3x) on pool eu1-dedicated-pool-3 node group. jonathan_eng: Can you paste a sample of the kernel log? kevin_sre: sure, snippet below from node gpu-ef-12 (last 24h):
```
Nov 10 02:12:01 gpu-ef-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Nov 10 02:12:02 gpu-ef-12 kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (1)
Nov 10 05:03:40 gpu-ef-12 kernel: Correctable ECC error detected on memory-bank 3
```
maria_cs: Thanks. This will impact a small number of Dedicated and Private customers in eu-west if we need to replace cards. Need a short customer note draft for affected tenants. sara_csm: Agreement — keep it proactive and options-first: scheduled rolling replacements with failover routing, expected 15–30m per node, minimal/no action for most customers. kevin_sre: Proposed operational plan: drain affected hosts, failover to warm spare capacity in eu1, attempt hot-swap replacement during a maintenance window, rollback to original host after QA, full replacement if instability persists. jonathan_eng: Technical details for the note: probable cause = increasing correctable ECC due to degraded DIMM or GPU memory; trigger for full replacement = repeat Xid 79 or uncorrectable ECC. We can mitigate by migrating customer workloads to warm spares. ops_bot: [metric] warm-spare-utilization: currently 40% in eu1, headroom for rolling replacements. maria_cs: Draft for customers (short):

"Hello — we’re performing proactive maintenance for a small set of Dedicated/Private GPU hosts in eu-west. Our monitoring detected elevated correctable ECC counts and intermittent Xid events on a subset of devices. To prevent customer impact we’ll be: 
• Draining affected hosts and moving workloads to warm spare capacity. 
• Performing hot-swap replacement of the GPU hardware. 
• Validating workloads and returning traffic after testing.

Estimated impact: most customers will see no disruption. For a small number of builds you may observe a single short failover (approx 15–30 minutes). We’ll notify you before any host-level maintenance and provide an incident summary after the work. If you have strict affinity or pinned model versions, reply and we’ll run a no-migration option and schedule a dedicated maintenance window.

Contact: support@redwood.ai or reply here and we’ll coordinate"

sara_csm: Nice. Add an option for customers that require IP/network affinity to request a maintenance window instead of automatic failover. Also include a link to our runbook for dedicated failover: https://intranet.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-failover jonathan_eng: Add a very short technical addendum for SRE: rollback criteria = increased request errors post-rebalance >0.5% for 10m or repeated Xid 79 after replacement. kevin_sre: Proposed timeline: notify customers by EOD CET, perform rolling drains next Tue/Wed between 02:00–06:00 CET, 1–2 nodes per window to keep warm-spare headroom. ops_bot: [sched] maintenance windows reserved: 2026-11-17 02:00-06:00 CET and 2026-11-18 02:00-06:00 CET. maria_cs: Final send draft (shorter, customer-facing):

"Maintenance notice — proactive hardware replacement in eu-west
We detected intermittent GPU memory errors on a small set of Reserved/Dedicated hosts in eu-west. To prevent any interruption we will perform proactive rolling replacements and migrate workloads to spare capacity.
When: Nov 17–18, 02:00–06:00 CET (we will only touch 1–2 hosts per window).
Impact: expected minimal. You may see a short failover (15–30m) if your workloads are running on an affected host.
If you require zero migration/affinity, reply and we’ll schedule a targeted window.
Contact: support@redwood.ai"

sara_csm: :thumbsup: send when ready. kevin_sre: I’ll post to the affected tenant list and the status page, and set an alert to pause replacements if warm-spare headroom drops below 15%. jonathan_eng: After replacements we’ll run a quick perf regression on 5% of traffic and rollback if token latency P95 increases >10% or error rate bump. kevin_sre: logging note for postmortem — collect ECC counts, Xid traces, nvml health output, and physical GPU serials. ops_bot: [note] created support ticket TCK-45891 and internal job replacing GPUs in group eu1-dedicated-pool-3. Last update will be posted to status.redwood.ai. maria_cs: sending final customer messages now, copying affected CSMs. End of thread.
